  Today's Topic Summary

Group: http://groups.google.com/group/r-inla-discussion-group/topics

  • Nested random effects [1 Update]
 Nested random effects
    Julin Maloof <jnma...@gmail.com> Sep 28 12:59PM -0700  

    Hello,
     
    I am trying to figure out how to specify nested random effects in INLA and
    would also like to estimate the variance components of such effects. I
    have started by trying to implement some of the simple examples from
    Pinheiro and Bates. I have two questions:
     
    1) When I calculate the standard dev attributable to a random effect (using
    inla.contrib.sd()) the estimates are similar to those from lme when the
    Maximum Likelihood method is used, and are shrunk relative to an lme fit
    with REML. Is it possible to obtain estimates from an inla fit that are
    more in line with those produced by using REML in lme?
     
    2) How can nested random effects be specified?
     
    The code below illustrates these questions.
     
    Thanks,
     
    Julin
     
    library(INLA)
    library(nlme)
    data(Machines)
    ?Machines #3 machines, each tested by 6 workers.

    m <- as.data.frame(Machines) #so that we have the same format going into
    lme and inla
    head(m)
     
    lme1 <- lme(score ~ Machine,random=~1|Worker,data=m)
    summary(lme1)
     
    inla1 <- inla(score ~ Machine + f(Worker,model="iid"),data=m)
    summary(inla1)
    inla.contrib.sd(inla1)$hyper
    #INLA and lme similar but sd estimates for the random effects are smaller
    from INLA.
    #Why? INLA estimates are similar to Maximum Likelihood estimates in lme:
     
    lme1b <- lme(score ~ Machine,random=~1|Worker,data=m,method="ML")
    VarCorr(lme1b)
     
    ##What about a nested model? We nest Machine inside of Worker to estimate
    the
    #variance of workers on different machines
    lme2 <- lme(score ~ Machine,random=~1|Worker/Machine,data=m,method="ML")
    summary(lme2)
    VarCorr(lme2)
     
    #unsure how to do this in INLA
    #separate random effects don't work:
    inla2 <- inla(score ~ Machine + f(Worker,model="iid") +
    f(Machine,model="iid"),data=m)
    summary(inla2)
    inla.contrib.sd(inla2)$hyper
     
    ##Could make a new term that represents the machine.worker combo
    m$machine.worker <- paste(m$Machine,m$Worker,sep=".")
    inla2b <- inla(score ~ Machine + f(Worker,model="iid") +
    f(machine.worker,model="iid"),data=m)
    summary(inla2b)
    inla.contrib.sd(inla2b)$hyper
    VarCorr(lme2) #lme has larger variance for Machine than inla
     
    ##note that lme4 can handle this type of specfication
    detach("package:nlme")
    library(lme4)
     
    lmer2 <- lmer(score ~ Machine + (1|Worker) +
    (1|machine.worker),data=m,REML=F)
    summary(lmer2)
